text_summary.body: Priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua; the line Jeshua, Joiakim, Eliashib, Joiada, Jonathan, Jaddua; the heads of priestly houses in the days of Joiakim; Levites and priests recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, in the reign of Darius the Persian; Levites written in the book of the chronicles to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib; the Levitical heads who served in the days of Joiakim, Nehemiah and Ezra.

setting.period: From 538 BC to the late fifth (or late fourth) century BC
setting.body: Johanan is high priest in 408/407 (Cowley 30). Keil takes "Darius the Persian" as Darius II (424–404) and the list of 12:22 as one enrolment while Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and the young Jaddua were alive. Josephus makes Jaddua high priest under Darius III and Alexander; Cowley calls 12:22–23 a later addition.

constraints.textual_assertion: in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe
assumptions: The registers run from the first return to the days of Johanan/Jaddua; anchored here by the reference to Nehemiah's days.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik presents the lists without discussing the date of Jaddua or Darius.

open_questions: The Samaria (Wadi Daliyeh) papyri and modern studies of the high-priestly succession were not consulted.
